title: Contextual Fallback Orchestrator for Pinned Revisions and Deprecation Windows
creator: Aisha Patel
description: Goal: provide an automated, observable orchestration layer that safely substitutes pinned model revisions when a pinned instance is unavailable, degraded, or entering a scheduled deprecation window. The orchestrator must use a compatibility score (semantic output similarity + API/shape checks), regional health, latency SLOs, and cost delta to decide substitution order, and must expose controls in the Console and API for operators and customers to opt into conservative or aggressive strategies. This ticket designs the policy layer, probes/warmup choreography, telemetry and alerting hooks, and the controlled rollout/deprecation path for pinned versions.
acceptance_criteria: Operator can choose fallthrough policy per pinned revision: strict-compatible-only | fast-failover | cost-aware | regional-preference
System computes and logs a compatibility_score for every candidate substitution; stored in trace and available in Console traces
Automated warmup probes (up to N probes per candidate) run before shifting >10% traffic to a substitute variant
Deprecation window API sends 14/7/1 day notices to customers with pinned revisions plus an actionable change: choose fallback policy or request grandfathering
Fallback decisions are reversible and auditable; rollout must include telemetry showing success rate, latency delta, and quality regression metrics
Dashboard widgets for pinned revision health, active fallbacks, and compatibility distributions are created under runtime-1.23 release dashboards
proposed_solution: Introduce a Contextual Compatibility Scorer that evaluates: output-embedding cosine similarity on a small probe set, API surface compatibility (input/output fields), and runtime tokenization/length-preservation heuristics
Score = weighted sum (embedding_similarity: 0.6, api_shape: 0.2, latency_match: 0.2); thresholds configurable per customer
Fallback decision engine inputs: compatibility_score, region_health(score), current_latency_percentile, cost_multiplier, pinned_revision_deprecation_state
Traffic shift plan: probe -> 1% -> 10% -> 50% -> 100% with KV-cache prefill between steps; pause-and-rollback on quality regression > X or latency breach
Console and API: per-pinned-revision fallback_profile allowing customers to set policies and opt into automated migration windows
Deprecation process: phased notices, forced migration only after customer opt-out window; system support for extended grandfathering via support ticket
implementation_tasks: Runtime: add compatibility_probe API (internal) to run small deterministic inputs against candidate variants and return embed/signature
Orchestrator: implement decision graph and policy engine in control plane service; persist compatibility_score and decision context in traces
Serving runtime: add prefill KV-cache hook that can be invoked by orchestrator with rate-limited warmup traffic
Console: UI to display pinned revision health, view computed compatibility scores for candidate variants, and set per-revision fallback_profile
Docs/PR: update onboarding checklist with new fields: fallback_profile, deprecation_notifications, and compatibility_thresholds
E2E tests: simulate regional outage and run canary fallback scenario asserting no >10% user-visible regression in sample prompts
Telemetry: add metrics pinned.fallback.attempts, pinned.fallback.success_rate, compatibility_score.histogram, pinned.deprecation.notifications_sent
test_plan: Unit tests for compatibility scorer (embedding mock, api_shape matcher)
Integration test: orchestrator + runtime warmup hooks running in staging across us-east1/us-west1
Chaos test: simulate disk/oom on pinned model hosts and assert orchestrator performs failover according to chosen profile
Quality check: run Canary evaluation suite (100 canonical prompts) after each traffic increase step and compute BLEU/embedding-drift thresholds
rollout_plan: Phase 1 (staging): run orchestrator in dry-run mode for 2 weeks capturing decisions (no traffic shifts)
Phase 2 (limited): enable conservative policy for <10% of pinned customers, perform probe + staged traffic shift
Phase 3 (general): enable Console controls for all customers, start sending deprecation notices for pinned revisions older than 12 months
Rollback rules: automatic rollback on (a) compatibility_score below configurable limit, (b) 95th latency > SLO by 30% for 5 minutes, or (c) quality_regression_rate > 2% on canary prompts
notes: Trade-offs considered: aggressive cost-aware fallback reduces spend but may increase semantic regressions; defaulting to compatibility-first minimizes customer-visible regressions
We debated relying solely on embedding similarity vs. also running end-to-end structured-output checks; decided to combine both with weighted scoring
Open question: whether to allow customers to pin fallback candidate list explicitly (pros: deterministic; cons: increases customer support surface). Proposal: allow as opt-in field in Console
Coordination: must align with Support and Legal on deprecation notice language and grandfathering SLAs
Related internal discussions: runtime-ops on warmup cost accounting; cost of probes will be charged to owning org by default
